All industries ↗

Turn guidelines into a team plan

Grant work begins with a long document and becomes a shared effort across programs, development, finance, and leadership. Maia can extract stated requirements and dates, cite their pages, compare them with the application folder, and prepare a checklist in Slack.

The grant owner confirms eligibility, claims, budget, dates, and submission. Maia helps the team see what is missing and who needs to act.

Prepare the grant checklist

Supply the official guidelines, internal calendar, application folder, prior discussion, and your owner map. Ask Maia for every required section, attachment, deadline, formatting rule, and unanswered question.

The output can propose owners and reminder dates after the team confirms the source. An ambiguous requirement should stay attached to its quoted passage so staff can ask the funder or make a considered interpretation.

Draft donor follow-up from verified records

Give Maia the authorized constituent record, confirmed contribution details, and approved template. It can identify missing fields and draft an acknowledgement or follow-up for staff review.

Authorized staff verify the donor, contribution, required wording, and intended recipient before sending. Staff decide tax treatment and whether the final acknowledgement meets the applicable requirements.

Prepare program updates

Combine a selected program tracker, approved spreadsheets, documents, and channel decisions. Maia can prepare an internal brief with activity, milestones, blockers, decisions, and upcoming commitments.

The program lead corrects interpretation and chooses what to escalate. Sensitive beneficiary information should stay out of a broad channel; use summarized or non-sensitive records for shared updates.

Build a board packet brief

With approved reports, the agenda, prior decisions, and a reviewed finance summary, Maia can draft a source-linked digest and list unanswered questions. It can also carry action items from the previous meeting into the new agenda.

The executive director or board liaison approves the pack and distribution. Final financial, governance, and program claims remain with the people responsible for them.

Start with public grant guidelines

Choose one grant application and its official guideline document. Ask Maia to compare the application folder with the requirements, cite each page, and leave an ambiguous requirement with the grant owner before scheduling reminders.

After the grant meeting, Maia can turn the confirmed checklist into owner reminders and a short internal status update. The team can see which items depend on program, finance, development, or leadership and resolve conflicts before the final submission review.

The same pattern can support an event or board cycle. Start with the approved checklist, keep source dates visible, and bring only missing materials and decisions into the next channel update.

Questions from nonprofit teams

Can Maia help write grant applications?

It can prepare requirements, research notes, outlines, and drafts from supplied evidence. Staff own eligibility, claims, budgets, and submission.

Can Maia draft donor acknowledgements?

Yes, from verified constituent and contribution records plus an approved template. Authorized staff review the facts and wording before sending.

How is sensitive program or donor information handled?

Use only approved records and choose a channel audience allowed to see the output. Keep private beneficiary and donor details in restricted workflows.
